messages.text: The "single" test fails because when there's no dash in the input (e.g., `"7"`), `split("-")` returns an array with one element, so `to` is `undefined` and `Number(undefined)` is `NaN`. The fix is to handle the case where only a single number is provided.

response.text:
The failing test was "single" which tests parsing `"7"` (a single number without a dash). The root cause was in `parseRange`: when there's no `-` in the input, `split("-")` returns an array with only one element, so `to` is `undefined` and `Number(undefined)` produces `NaN`.

The fix: use `to ?? from` as the default value for `to`, so when parsing a single number like `"7"`, both `from` and `to` are set to `7`.
